Primary concerns are throughput guarantees during peak shift changes and a clear SLA for cross-region failover and data residency.

Procurement note: evaluating 12–24 month committed capacity. Wants clear credit/penalty language tied to p95 and availability.

Sales play: shift from proof-of-concept (chat+kb search) into Dedicated POC with 4-week stress test; include Optimize recommendations for quantization and batching to hit cost targets.

requirements_summary: Workload: operator chat (short-turn dialog, 8 tokens request avg, 200 token response avg), KB similarity search (dense embeddings), and telemetry reranking at commit time. Targets: p95 < 80ms for chat in-region, p95 < 200ms for embeddings, throughput 600 RPS sustained per region during peak with ~2x burst headroom. Residency: NA primary, EU backup (must not replicate PII outside NA without explicit opt-in). High-availability: cross-region failover with <30s RTO for chat endpoints and transparent routing fallback to quantized model variant when primary capacity saturated.
technical_questions: Can Redwood guarantee p95 latency at 600 RPS on Dedicated size X? Provide benchmark data (token lengths specified)
How is KV cache warmed across regions during failover? What is cold-start penalty?
What are model variant compatibility guarantees (LLM->smaller quantized variant) for chat prompt fidelity during fallback?
Are automatic fallbacks tunable by customer (latency vs quality thresholds)?
